<workout_file>
  <name>Abrahamsen Sweetspot-Threshold</name>
  <description>Jonas Abrahamsen sweetspot-to-threshold session: 2hr progressive ladder of 6min efforts at 87%, 91%, 95% and 100% FTP, each done twice with 6min recovery at 50% FTP. Builds threshold durability. Powers given directly as %FTP in the source.</description>
  <author>https://www.trainingpeaks.com/training-plans/cycling/tp-619690/train-like-the-pros-7-pro-cyclist-training-sessions</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="960" PowerLow="0.35" PowerHigh="0.75" />
    <SteadyState Duration="240" Power="0.5" />
    <IntervalsT Repeat="2" OnDuration="360" OffDuration="360" OnPower="0.87" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <IntervalsT Repeat="2" OnDuration="360" OffDuration="360" OnPower="0.91" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <IntervalsT Repeat="2" OnDuration="360" OffDuration="360" OnPower="0.95" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <IntervalsT Repeat="2" OnDuration="360" OffDuration="360" OnPower="1.0" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <Cooldown Duration="240" PowerLow="0.5" PowerHigh="0.44" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>

  <description>Kristin Armstrong "Turn Up The Heat" session: a 1min step ladder from 60% to 120% FTP, then three rounds of 3min@93% FTP with a 1min@110% surge followed by 1min recovery. Powers given directly as %FTP in the source.</description>

  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>

    <SteadyState Duration="60" Power="0.6" />
    <SteadyState Duration="60" Power="0.7" />
    <SteadyState Duration="60" Power="0.8" />
    <SteadyState Duration="60" Power="0.9" />

    <SteadyState Duration="60" Power="1.1" />
    <SteadyState Duration="60" Power="1.2" />

</workout_file>

<workout_file>
  <name>McNulty Base Endurance</name>
  <description>Brandon McNulty's steady base endurance ride. In his 12/15/21 base ride, 79% of the time was spent in Zone 2, ridden steadily at ~65% of FTP (271 W). Ride duration is not given in the source, so this is modeled as a 3-hour steady ride.</description>
  <author>https://www.evoq.bike/blog/train-like-a-pro</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="600" PowerLow="0.5" PowerHigh="0.65" />
    <SteadyState Duration="9600" Power="0.65" />
    <Cooldown Duration="600" PowerLow="0.65" PowerHigh="0.5" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>

<workout_file>
  <name>McNulty Lactate Clearance</name>
  <description>Brandon McNulty's lactate clearance session (8/9/22): 2x20 minute intervals at ~FTP (420 W), alternating 4 minutes just below FTP and 1 minute surge at 110-115% of FTP. Recovery between the two blocks is modeled as 10 minutes easy.</description>
  <author>https://www.evoq.bike/blog/train-like-a-pro</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="600" PowerLow="0.5" PowerHigh="0.75" />
    <IntervalsT Repeat="4" OnDuration="240" OffDuration="60" OnPower="0.95" OffPower="1.12"/>
    <SteadyState Duration="600" Power="0.5" />
    <IntervalsT Repeat="4" OnDuration="240" OffDuration="60" OnPower="0.95" OffPower="1.12"/>
    <Cooldown Duration="600" PowerLow="0.65" PowerHigh="0.5" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>

<workout_file>
  <name>McNulty Low Cadence Torque</name>
  <description>Brandon McNulty's low cadence torque session (12/11/21): 8x4 minute intervals at ~90% of FTP (370 W) at 40 rpm, for muscular endurance and fiber type conversion. Rest between intervals is not specified, so it is modeled as 3 minutes easy.</description>
  <author>https://www.evoq.bike/blog/train-like-a-pro</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="600" PowerLow="0.5" PowerHigh="0.7" />
    <IntervalsT Repeat="8" OnDuration="240" OffDuration="180" OnPower="0.9" OffPower="0.5" Cadence="40"/>
    <Cooldown Duration="600" PowerLow="0.65" PowerHigh="0.5" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>

<workout_file>
  <name>McNulty Race Prep</name>
  <description>Brandon McNulty's race-specific interval session (1/22/22) ahead of Trofeo Calvia: 3x10 minute intervals. The first is 10 minutes at 500 W (~120% FTP); the next two are 5 minutes at FTP straight into 40/20 efforts. 40/20 on-power is not specified, so it is modeled at ~130% FTP.</description>
  <author>https://www.evoq.bike/blog/train-like-a-pro</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="600" PowerLow="0.5" PowerHigh="0.8" />
    <SteadyState Duration="600" Power="1.2" />
    <SteadyState Duration="300" Power="0.5" />
    <SteadyState Duration="300" Power="1.0" />
    <IntervalsT Repeat="5" OnDuration="40" OffDuration="20" OnPower="1.3" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <SteadyState Duration="300" Power="0.5" />
    <SteadyState Duration="300" Power="1.0" />
    <IntervalsT Repeat="5" OnDuration="40" OffDuration="20" OnPower="1.3" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <Cooldown Duration="600" PowerLow="0.65" PowerHigh="0.5" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>

<workout_file>
  <name>McNulty Recovery Ride</name>
  <description>Brandon McNulty's recovery ride (5/13/22): 90 minutes at 188 W, well below 50% of FTP (~45%), to get blood flowing and prevent staleness in the legs.</description>
  <author>https://www.evoq.bike/blog/train-like-a-pro</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="300" PowerLow="0.4" PowerHigh="0.45" />
    <SteadyState Duration="4800" Power="0.45" />
    <Cooldown Duration="300" PowerLow="0.45" PowerHigh="0.4" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>

<workout_file>
  <name>McNulty Tempo</name>
  <description>Brandon McNulty's monster base-season tempo workout (12/20/21): 3x60 minute intervals at ~80-85% of FTP (360 W). The full session ran about 4.5 hours with 323 W normalized power and 5,097 kJ. Recovery between intervals is modeled as 25 minutes easy.</description>
  <author>https://www.evoq.bike/blog/train-like-a-pro</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="1200" PowerLow="0.5" PowerHigh="0.8" />
    <SteadyState Duration="3600" Power="0.85" />
    <SteadyState Duration="1500" Power="0.55" />
    <SteadyState Duration="3600" Power="0.85" />
    <SteadyState Duration="1500" Power="0.55" />
    <SteadyState Duration="3600" Power="0.85" />
    <Cooldown Duration="1200" PowerLow="0.6" PowerHigh="0.5" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>

<workout_file>
  <name>McNulty VO2max</name>
  <description>Brandon McNulty's classic VO2max interval session (4/5/22): 4x4 minute intervals at 500 W (~120% of FTP) with long rest to achieve maximal power on each interval. Rest is modeled as 5 minutes easy.</description>
  <author>https://www.evoq.bike/blog/train-like-a-pro</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="600" PowerLow="0.5" PowerHigh="0.75" />
    <IntervalsT Repeat="4" OnDuration="240" OffDuration="300" OnPower="1.2" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <Cooldown Duration="600" PowerLow="0.65" PowerHigh="0.5" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>

<workout_file>
  <name>Roglic Under-Over</name>
  <description>Primoz Roglic under/over threshold session: four blocks of 4x (20sec @125% FTP / 40sec @100% FTP), each block separated by 5min at 50% FTP. Trains ability to clear lactate and sustain efforts at/above threshold. Powers given directly as %FTP in the source.</description>

<workout_file>
  <name>Simmons Breakaway Simulation</name>
  <description>Quinn Simmons' breakaway simulation: 5x6 min at ~400W (~89% FTP), immediately into fat-max endurance (~340W, ~76% FTP), mimicking the fight to make a breakaway then rolling turns once it sticks. FTP assumed 450W.</description>
  <author>https://www.evoq.bike/blog/inside-the-training</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="600" PowerLow="0.5" PowerHigh="0.75" />
    <IntervalsT Repeat="5" OnDuration="360" OffDuration="360" OnPower="0.89" OffPower="0.76"/>
    <Cooldown Duration="600" PowerLow="0.6" PowerHigh="0.5" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>

<workout_file>
  <name>Simmons FatMax Race Simulation</name>
  <description>Quinn Simmons' fatigue-resistance session: 4.5 hours at ~340W (~75% FTP, fat-max zone), then 2x30/30s max efforts to simulate a late-race breakaway. FTP assumed 450W; the "max" efforts are modeled at ~120% FTP.</description>
  <author>https://www.evoq.bike/blog/inside-the-training</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="600" PowerLow="0.5" PowerHigh="0.75" />
    <SteadyState Duration="16200" Power="0.75" />
    <IntervalsT Repeat="2" OnDuration="30" OffDuration="30" OnPower="1.2" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <Cooldown Duration="600" PowerLow="0.6" PowerHigh="0.5" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>

<workout_file>
  <name>Simmons Low Cadence Strength</name>
  <description>Quinn Simmons' low-cadence strength session: 7x10 min at 360-390W (modeled at ~375W, ~83% FTP) at 50 RPM, targeting muscle recruitment and his identified "weakness zone." FTP assumed 450W. Rest modeled as 3 min easy.</description>
  <author>https://www.evoq.bike/blog/inside-the-training</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="600" PowerLow="0.5" PowerHigh="0.75" />
    <IntervalsT Repeat="7" OnDuration="600" OffDuration="180" OnPower="0.83" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <Cooldown Duration="600" PowerLow="0.6" PowerHigh="0.5" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>

<workout_file>
  <name>Simmons VO2 Max Death March</name>
  <description>Quinn Simmons' "VO2 death march" (sea level): 5x3 min, 4x3 min, then 4x2 min all-out at 540-550W (~120% FTP), with full recovery (~3 min) between intervals. FTP assumed 450W.</description>
  <author>https://www.evoq.bike/blog/inside-the-training</author>
  <sportType>bike</sportType>
  <workout>
    <Warmup Duration="600" PowerLow="0.5" PowerHigh="0.75" />
    <IntervalsT Repeat="5" OnDuration="180" OffDuration="180" OnPower="1.2" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <IntervalsT Repeat="4" OnDuration="180" OffDuration="180" OnPower="1.2" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <IntervalsT Repeat="4" OnDuration="120" OffDuration="180" OnPower="1.2" OffPower="0.5"/>
    <Cooldown Duration="600" PowerLow="0.6" PowerHigh="0.5" />
  </workout>
</workout_file>
